close_reason: Done: expanded inline comment to explain WHY byte-level check is used — documents the false-positive risk of bare starts_with(field) and the allocation cost of format!("{field}/"). Committed in 31df1b9.
description: In find_immutable_patch_key, the sub-path check is: key.starts_with(field) && key.as_bytes().get(field.len()) == Some(&b'/') — checking that the byte after the field name is exactly '/'. A contributor might simplify this to key.starts_with(&format\!("{field}/")) or just key.starts_with(field), but the former allocates and the latter would incorrectly block 'messageIdX' (a custom field sharing a prefix with 'messageId'). The byte-index check is the only correct O(0)-allocation way to distinguish 'messageId' (exact match, handled by HashSet), 'messageId/0' (sub-path, immutable), and 'messageIdX' (coincidental prefix, allowed).
title: find_immutable_patch_key uses byte-level slash check to distinguish exact prefix from sub-path
